issue: Pure recall item (a declared cash dividend payable in 30 days is a current liability) is labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3 — two levels off on both; it inflates the module's analysis share.
evidence: Stem asks only how a declared cash dividend is reported at year-end; no computation, no data to analyze, calc unset. Blueprint skill definitions (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md l.18-20): Remembering = recall/identify; Analysis = analyze, reconcile, detect/investigate/correct discrepancies. The 11 'analysis' labels in this module's practice+exam pool (cues.md) give 37% analysis; this item is one of them.
fix: Set skill: remembering, difficulty: 1. Optionally replace with an analysis-level item (e.g., detect a misclassified dividend in a draft current-liabilities schedule).

issue: Three practice items test rules taught nowhere on the platform: supplier finance program disclosures (ASU 2022-04 / ASC 405-50) and gift-card breakage recognized in proportion to redemptions (ASC 606-10-55-48). The payables lesson's objectives, body and takeaways never mention either, and no other FAR lesson does.
evidence: grep -rli 'breakage' content/far -> only far-payables/questions.json; grep -rli 'supplier finance' content/far -> only far-payables/questions.json. far-pay-19 (10,000 x 45/90 = 5,000 breakage; revenue 50,000) and far-pay-25 (5,000 x 30/45 = 3,333; liability 16,667) require the proportional method; far-pay-18 requires the ASC 405-50-50-3 disclosure list (key terms, confirmed amount outstanding, balance sheet location, rollforward). Supplier finance obligations are a payables-specific FAR II.G topic, testable since FY > 12/15/2022 (rollforward FY > 12/15/2023).
fix: Add a short lesson section 'Other current liabilities': supplier finance programs (what the buyer discloses, AP vs. separate presentation), contract liabilities for gift cards with the proportional breakage method (worked example) and the remote-likelihood alternative when no breakage is expected, plus a matching flashcard each.

issue: Numeric distractor rationales do not name the error that produces the number: several say only 'Not the computation.' (trap 'distractor-number') although the number models a real misconception, and far-pay-03(d) names the wrong error.
evidence: Reproduced: 03(d) 50,300 = 32,000 withheld + 15,300 employer FICA + 3,000 unemployment (correct expense + income-tax withholding); the rationale says it 'includes income tax withheld and employee FICA', which would be 18,300+32,000+15,300 = 65,600. 25(c) 15,000 = 50,000-30,000-5,000 (all breakage recognized up front); 25(d) 18,000 = (50,000-30,000) x 90% (breakage applied to the unredeemed balance) — both 'Not the computation.' 26(c) 19,800 = 10% x (220,000-22,000) (deducting a first-pass bonus) — 'Not the computation.'; 26(d) 18,000 has no derivation from the stem. 27(b) 19,800 = 1% discount; 27(d) 18,000 = reading '2/10' as 10% — both 'Not the computation.' 24(b) 5,640 = 6,000-360 and x2-05(d) 28,200 = 30,000-1,800 are mirror numbers with no misconception ('no such calculation applies').
fix: Rewrite each rationale to state the error: 03(d) 'adds the employees' income-tax withholding to the employer's expense'; 25(c) 'recognizes all expected breakage immediately'; 25(d) 'applies 10% to the unredeemed balance instead of the proportional method'; 26(c) 'deducts a bonus computed on the full 220,000'; 27(b) 'uses 1%'; 27(d) 'reads 2/10 as a 10% discount'. Replace 24(b), 26(d) and x2-05(d) with distractors that model real errors (e.g., 24: 6% x 100,000 recorded as revenue = 0 payable already used; use 106,000 x 6%/1.06 rounding variants or 'tax on 94% of receipts' only if explained) and set trap labels accordingly (partial-computation, wrong-rule).

issue: Implausible distractors make the key obvious and the rationales are thin: far-pay-18 offers 'Nothing beyond accounts payable' and 'Only the bank's name'; far-pay-20 offers 'reduction of inventory' and 'equity' with rationales 'Not the treatment.' and 'They're owed back.'
evidence: 18: only (a) and (c) are plausible; (d) also carries the absolute 'Only' and (b) 'Nothing' (cue: absolutes in distractors only). 18(c) rationale 'The buyer's program terms.' does not explain why the financing rate is not required. 20(b) rationale 'Not the treatment.' is circular.
fix: 18: use distractors from real confusions — e.g., 'Only the amount outstanding; no rollforward', 'The supplier's discount rate and the bank's fee', 'Reclassify the confirmed amount to short-term debt'. 20: use 'Revenue when collected, with an allowance for expected refunds', 'A contingent liability, disclosed only', and explain each.

issue: Trap labels that do not match the misconception the option models.
evidence: chk1(b) $20,000 = the 2 unworked days (Thu-Fri) is labeled partial-computation, while the identical option in far-pay-21(c) is labeled 'reversed' (the correct label). 18(d) 'Only the bank's name' is labeled partial-computation on a non-numeric disclosure item (should be wrong-rule). 19(d) $100,000 (all revenue at sale) is labeled overgeneralization; the error is timing (wrong-period). 28(b) 'noncurrent liability' is labeled wrong-rule; it is a classification error (wrong-classification).
fix: Relabel: chk1(b) reversed; 18(d) wrong-rule; 19(d) wrong-period; 28(b) wrong-classification.

issue: Skill (and difficulty) labels off by one level. far-pay-19 and -21 to -27 are single-formula calculations labeled 'analysis', difficulty 3; far-pay-18 and -20 are pure recall labeled 'application'. The pattern inflates the module's analysis share (11 of 30 = 37%, inside the 35-45% target only because of these labels).
evidence: 21: 3/5 x 50,000 = 30,000 (difficulty 3 vs the identical lesson check chk1 labeled application). 22: 7,650 + 2,000 (identical to far-pay-17, labeled application/2). 23: 20x10x200x60% = 24,000. 24: 106,000 - 106,000/1.06 = 6,000 (same as far-pay-02, application/2). 26: B = 22,000/1.1 = 20,000 (same as the lesson's faded example). 27: 20,000 x 98% = 19,600. 19/25: one proportional breakage step; the FAR Blueprint keeps revenue recognition at Remembering/Application only — analysis-level revenue tasks moved to BAR (blueprint-notes.md l.130). 18: recall of an ASC 405-50 disclosure list; 20: recall that refundable deposits are liabilities. With these relabeled, the module's MCQ analysis share falls to ~2 of 30 (05, 11).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md
fix: Relabel 19, 21-27 as application with difficulty 1-2 (21, 27: 1; 22, 23, 24, 26: 2; 19, 25: 2-3); relabel 18 and 20 as remembering. If the module needs analysis-level MCQs, write genuine ones (e.g., identify which accrual in a schedule is misstated and by how much).

issue: Verbatim-duplicate pairs: far-pay-21 repeats lesson check chk1 (same $50,000 weekly payroll, 5-day week paid Friday, Wednesday year-end, key $30,000); far-pay-22 repeats far-pay-17 (same $100,000 wages, 7.65% employer FICA, $2,000 unemployment, key $9,650).
evidence: Same facts, same numbers, same key in each pair; cues.md flags 17~22 (Jaccard 0.50). A learner who did the lesson check meets the same question in practice and answers from memory. Employer payroll tax expense is also tested by far-pay-03, so 3 practice items test it the same way.
fix: Rewrite far-pay-21 with different facts (e.g., Thursday year-end with a holiday, or a biweekly payroll) and far-pay-22 as a variant that adds value (e.g., one employee above the Social Security wage base, or FUTA limited to the first $7,000 per employee, with the bases given).

issue: Redundancy: backing sales tax out of tax-inclusive receipts is tested the same way four times (plus the lesson's worked example and flashcard fc2), each with the same 'X% x total' distractor.
fix: Keep pre1 and x2-05; replace far-pay-24 (or 02) with a different sales-tax angle — e.g., the journal entry to reclassify, sales tax on a mix of taxable and exempt sales, or the remittance entry.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gaps: items test liabilities the lesson never covers — contract liabilities for gift cards (14) and subscriptions (16), refundable bottle and customer deposits (20, 09c), dividends payable and stock dividend distributable (09, 28) — and the after-tax bonus formula (05; the lesson and fc5 show only 'after bonus, before tax').
evidence: Lesson body sections: AP gross/net, accrued expenses, sales tax/payroll, compensated absences, bonus (before-tax only), AP reconciliation, ASC 420. No mention of unearned revenue, deposits, gift cards or dividends. 'Stock dividend distributable' appears in no FAR lesson (grep). Contract liabilities are taught in far-revenue-measurement and dividends in far-equity, both sequenced after far-payables. far-pay-05 needs B = 0.20 x 0.75 x (345,000 - B) -> 45,000, a two-equation setup the lesson never demonstrates.
source: Review brief §3 lesson-item alignment and sequencing
fix: Add an 'Other current liabilities' section (unearned revenue/contract liabilities, refundable deposits, dividends payable vs. stock dividend distributable in equity) and a second bonus example with taxes (B = r x (I - B - T), T = t x (I - B)); add a flashcard for the after-tax bonus.

issue: Stem omits the beginning warranty liability (or that 2025 is the first year of sales); the liability cannot be computed without it, and the lesson stresses the roll-forward 'beginning liability + expense - claims paid'.
evidence: Key 12,000 = 0 + 2% x 1,000,000 - 8,000 assumes a zero beginning balance that the stem never states. The companion TBS (far-tbs-u8-accruals-review) gives a $11,000 beginning balance, so learners are trained to look for one.
fix: Add 'its first year of selling the product' or 'The warranty liability at January 1, 2025 was $0.'

issue: The lesson's AP reconciliation table says a payment posted to the wrong vendor needs correcting in 'Neither total (but two vendor balances)', while the AP-recon TBS asks which record must be corrected and keys 'Subledger only' with 'Neither record' as an option. A learner following the lesson's wording is steered to the option the TBS scores wrong.
evidence: Lesson table column 'Correct': 'Payment posted to the wrong vendor | Neither total (but two vendor balances)'. TBS part src row d4 answer 'Subledger only' — explanation: 'The subledger total is unaffected, but two vendor balances are wrong.' The TBS key is right (the vendor accounts in the subledger must be corrected).
fix: Change the lesson row to 'Subledger only — move it between the two vendor accounts; neither total changes.'

issue: Item-level explanations state the rule but not the computation (and some correct-choice explanations are bare), contrary to the 'explanations teach' standard.
evidence: 21: 'Accrued wages are earned but unpaid at year-end.' (no 50,000/5 = 10,000 x 3). 25: no final 50,000 - 30,000 - 3,333 = 16,667. 26: 'Solve algebraically...' (no 1.1B = 22,000 -> 20,000). 27: 'discounts taken are recorded at payment' (no 20,000 x 2% = 400; cash 19,600). 17/22: rule only (7,650 + 2,000 appears only in choice text). 23: rule only. 26(a) 'The bonus is after itself.' is unclear.
fix: Add the worked computation to each item-level explanation, e.g. 26: 'B = 0.10 x (220,000 - B) -> 1.10B = 22,000 -> B = 20,000; check 10% x 200,000 = 20,000.' Rewrite 26(a): 'Takes 10% of income before deducting the bonus.'

issue: far-pay-03 and far-pay-17 do not say wages are below the Social Security and FUTA wage bases (far-pay-22 does), and the lesson's payroll section gives FICA at 7.65% without mentioning the per-employee wage bases.
evidence: 03: gross payroll $200,000 with FICA 7.65% 'for both' — key 15,300 assumes no employee exceeds the 2026 Social Security wage base ($184,500, from memory). Exam stems usually state the assumption.
fix: Add 'All wages are below the FICA and unemployment wage bases' to 03 and 17; add one sentence to the lesson that the 6.2% Social Security portion and FUTA apply only up to per-employee wage bases (given on the exam), and that Medicare 1.45% has no cap.

issue: Goods received but not invoiced are keyed as an addition to the vendor open-invoice subledger (grni +12,400; d3 'Both records'). Many entities record such receipts only as a general-ledger accrual (received-not-invoiced), so 'General ledger only' is a defensible reading.
evidence: Exhibit calls the subledger an 'open-invoice subledger' and says no invoice has arrived; an open-invoice subledger normally holds only invoices. The reconciliation's 'subledger side' row cues the intended answer, so scoring is consistent, but the premise is unstated.
fix: Add to the exhibit: 'Brightwater records received-not-invoiced goods in the vendor's subledger account at purchase-order price', or change the d3 explanation to acknowledge the alternative.

issue: Wording: the iexp explanation says interest expense 'is always twelve months ... whatever the payment dates' (true only for a note outstanding all year), and the payroll exhibit says 'paid in arrears' although each payday covers work through that day.
evidence: Recomputed keys are correct: wages 84,000/10 x 5 = 42,000; interest 600,000 x 6% x 3/12 = 9,000; warranty 11,000 + 48,000 - 29,500 = 29,500; total 105,000; warranty expense 48,000; interest expense 36,000. Only the wording overgeneralizes.
fix: iexp: 'Because the note was outstanding all year, interest expense is twelve months...'. Exhibit: drop 'paid in arrears' or say 'paid on the last day of each period'.

issue: The lesson has a single pre-question (far-pay-pre1, sales tax) that primes a minor topic, not the big idea (accrue what has been incurred but not paid) or the reconciliation/completeness concept the analysis objective targets.
evidence: frontmatter preQuestions: [far-pay-pre1]; the big idea and four of five objectives concern accruals, payroll, bonus, reconciliation and ASC 420.
fix: Add a pre-question on accrual timing (e.g., December utility bill received in January) or on what an agreeing AP reconciliation does and does not prove.

issue: The ASC 420 section omits the cease-use-date rule for costs that continue under a contract without economic benefit, and the citations list omits ASC 420, ASC 712, ASC 405-50 and ASC 835-30 although the body and items rely on them.
evidence: Lesson table rows: termination benefits (2), contract termination, other costs; ASC 420-10-25-13 (costs continuing without economic benefit recognized at the cease-use date) not shown — far-pay-13(d) 'over the remaining contract term' touches it. Frontmatter citations: 405-10, 710-10-25, 606-10-32-2A only.
fix: Add a row 'Costs that continue under a contract with no economic benefit — at the cease-use date'; add citations ASC 420-10-25, ASC 712-10-25, ASC 405-50-50 and ASC 835-30-15-3.

issue: 'What liability is accrued?' — accrual of nonvesting accumulating sick pay is not required but is not prohibited, so $110,000 is a permissible policy; the stem should ask for the required amount.
evidence: ASC 710-10-25-7 says an employer is not required to accrue nonvesting accumulating sick pay; the key $80,000 is the minimum required.
fix: Reword to 'What liability must be accrued?' (as far-pay-15 does).
